# Issue #17 Authority evidence packet

## Identity

Primary authority input: GitHub issue #17 snapshot supplied separately and sealed by Recorder.

## Clauses

A1 — A malformed Reviewer-generated Standards/Spec child prompt must be detected before either child starts and before the exactly-once sibling batch is consumed.

A2 — Both child prompts must remain traceable to the canonical external code-review Skill, opaque caller task, fixed review range, and axis-specific evidence burden. Standards and Spec remain isolated.

A3 — Preflight rejection/correction is not a started Reviewer Agent sibling batch. Once either child starts, the existing exactly-one sibling-batch law remains unchanged.

A4 — Existing post-run compliance audit remains responsible for proving actual dispatched prompt identity, fixed-target traceability, axis isolation, successful child evidence, and faithful aggregation. Preflight must not become a second semantic reviewer.

A5 — Durable evidence binds either each exact compiled prompt or a deterministic recipe/version plus exact inputs and SHA-256. It does not retain generic session/tool-event payloads.

A6 — No Fowler baseline text, prompt templates, schema/CLI mechanics, or task-specific policy enters Reviewer Soul. No role topology, caller-owned ordering/repetition, or cross-model-panel behavior is introduced.

## Counterexamples

C1 — Standards prompt abbreviates the canonical baseline-smell definitions/remedies; children run; post-run auditor refuses; the unique batch is irrecoverably consumed.

C2 — Opaque task accidentally imposes an impossible executable allowlist; useful children run but the invocation can only refuse afterward.

C3 — Preflight starts one child before validating the sibling, so a rejected second prompt has already consumed part of the atomic batch.

C4 — Preflight accepts semantically blended prompts because it checks only nonblank strings/digests.

C5 — A model-based preflight becomes another post-hoc reviewer, adds nondeterminism, and still consumes budget without ensuring exact prompt construction.

## Boundaries requiring Authority disposition

U1 — Interface seam: narrow the current Reviewer `Agent` interface or replace it with one atomic two-leg batch-dispatch interface.

U2 — Compilation ownership: which prompt portions can be deterministically compiled from canonical Skill/task/range, and which irreducible semantic checks remain in post-run audit.

U3 — Executable policy: structured capabilities versus caller free-text constraints, including how impossible allowlists fail before child start without granting over-broad access.

U4 — Correction law: whether the parent may correct a rejected preflight proposal within the same invocation, what the bounded limit is, and what evidence proves no child started.

U5 — Evidence identity: store exact prompts versus recipe/version plus canonical inputs, while retaining sufficient bytes to prove actual prompt equality.

## Requested judgment

Establish construction authority and resolve—or explicitly escalate—the five boundary choices. Do not prescribe shallow helper names or implementation details. Apply-level code/probes are not required at Authority posture.
